title: Lead Generation for Small Businesses: Hong Kong deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Collect only what a lead needs: name, phone, need, consent; store it safely.
Three languages in daily use: your page in two (Traditional Chinese and English) is the minimum.
Direct marketing needs a clear choice for the customer to say no; keep that record.
Cluster A, Online selling and marketing: Strong fit: customers shop on phones and expect delivery within a day. Compete on speed and service, not price.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Launch with 3 pilot clients and a go or no-go rule at day 30. Check with a local expert.
Three languages in daily use: your page in two (Traditional Chinese and English) is the minimum.
Compare three models: pay per lead, monthly retainer, pay per sale. Choose by risk and cost per lead.
Write HKD next to every number.

questions.q: In "Register and license Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Some activities need an extra licence (food, health, money, education centres). List yours before you take a first order. Check with a local expert.
Write HKD next to every number.
Say in plain words what you collect and why; give a way to see and correct it.
Payments: bank transfer and fast-payment apps first; give an instant receipt.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: The personal data ordinance sets six principles, from collection and use to security and access.
Written terms, rest days and paid leave follow the employment law; keep signed copies. Check with a local expert.
Three languages in daily use: your page in two (Traditional Chinese and English) is the minimum.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?

questions.q: In "Find and serve customers Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit well; many one-person firms need flexible support.
Three languages in daily use: your page in two (Traditional Chinese and English) is the minimum.
Trust: put the business registration number, a real address and a refund note on every page. Check with a local expert.
Close to the wider region: many small firms serve customers across the border, so shipping and data rules matter early. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Price, tax and money Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Freelancers are common; write scope, price and date in one page before work starts.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?
Show a proof case: leads before and after, with the cost per lead.
Employers usually pay a compulsory retirement-fund contribution for staff; budget it from the first hire.

questions.q: In "People and partners Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Add tax and duty explicitly; never bury them in a price. Check with a local expert.
Use a part-time caller and a freelance writer; write a call script and a reply time rule. Check with a local expert.
Break-even units = fixed monthly cost divided by contribution per unit; round up.
Keep a registered address and a named contact; a shared-office address is common for a first year.

questions.q: In "Launch plan and review Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write HKD next to every number.
Contribution per unit = price minus the cost of each unit.
Dates: first test, first order, first review.
Compare three models: pay per lead, monthly retainer, pay per sale. Choose by risk and cost per lead.
